target.title: fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inferred commitments could accept an impossible calendar date from model output. For example, `2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z` was normalized into May and could persist a check-in for a date the model never validly expressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Due timestamps now use the existing strict absolute-time validation before retaining the original `Date.parse` result, preserving current timezone behavior. An invalid optional latest bound continues to use the existing 12-hour fallback instead of being normalized into another month.

This PR was AI-assisted. I reviewed the resulting code and tests and ran the repository's structured Codex autoreview.

Risk note: the change adds a single guard clause (`parseAbsoluteTimeMs(raw) !== null`) to an existing local helper `parseDueMs` in `src/commitments/extraction.ts:256`, reusing an established strict parser (`src/cron/parse.ts:65`) that shipped in v2026.6.9. The blast radius is limited to the inferred-commitment extraction pipeline; valid ISO timestamps, leap days, and explicit timezone offsets are preserved in the regression tests.

## User Impact

Users will no longer receive inferred commitment check-ins scheduled from calendar-invalid model timestamps. Valid leap-day and explicit timezone-offset timestamps continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Exact-head configured-model extraction, parsing, and persistence after review

I ran an uncommitted local proof harness from the public PR head. It used the production `buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt` and `parseCommitmentExtractionOutput`, the configured DeepSeek provider through `runEmbeddedAgent`, and the exact-head runtime queue, candidate validation, and commitment store. The validation control appended to the production prompt forced the model to return the three timestamp shapes under test; no candidate or persisted record was synthesized by the harness.

Command:

```
OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT=../openclaw-pr-106236-proof node --import tsx --no-warnings contrib/pr106236-exact-head-proof.mjs
```

Redacted output (configuration paths, prompt text, session ids, and credentials omitted):

```
[model-fetch] provider=deepseek model=deepseek-v4-pro status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
HEAD: 6e142f4360a05fa337985d51fdb3f1a4593ac34b
Configured model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
Runtime queue items processed: 3
Model candidates parsed: 3
MODEL proof:invalid-earliest: earliest=2027-04-31T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-04-31T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T09:00:00-08:00 latest=2028-02-29T12:00:00-08:00
Stored records: 2
STORE proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T05:00:00.000Z windowHours=12
STORE proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T17:00:00.000Z latest=2028-02-29T20:00:00.000Z windowHours=3
VERDICT: PASS — invalid earliest rejected; invalid latest fell back to 12h; valid leap-day offset persisted.
```

The store was isolated under a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and removed after the run. This proves the configured-model output crossed the exact-head parse, validation, and persistence boundaries: the impossible earliest date produced no stored record, the impossible optional latest bound used the existing 12-hour fallback, and the valid leap-day offset preserved its instants.

### Negative control — pre-fix gate accepts impossible calendar dates (real source functions)

`node --import tsx` drove the real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` against the pre-fix `parseDueMs` logic (Date.parse only):

```
Input: 2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z
Date.parse result: 1777654800000 (finite: true)
Date.parse builds: 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
parseAbsoluteTimeMs: null

Pre-fix gate:  Number.isFinite(parsed) only → ACCEPTED (BUG — normalized to May 1)
Post-fix gate: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parseAbsoluteTimeMs !== null → REJECTED (FIXED)
```

### Real-behavior proof — after fix (real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` + new `parseDueMs` logic)

Full proof harness exercising the real `src/cron/parse.ts` strict parser at `node --import tsx`:

```
========================================================================
  REAL-BEHAVIOR PROOF — PR #106236
  fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
========================================================================

PART 1 — parseAbsoluteTimeMs (the strict guard) raw output
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       parseAbsoluteTimeMs → null (REJECTED)
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       parseAbsoluteTimeMs → null (REJECTED)
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1835438400000
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z

PART 2 — BEFORE fix (old parseDueMs = Date.parse only)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       ACCEPTED → 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       ACCEPTED → 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  OLD totals: 5 accepted, 1 rejected

PART 3 — AFTER fix (new parseDueMs = Date.parse + strict parse)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       REJECTED (undefined)
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       REJECTED (undefined)
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  NEW totals: 3 accepted, 3 rejected

VERDICT
  Apr 31 rejected BEFORE fix: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to May 1)
  Apr 31 rejected AFTER  fix: YES ✓
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected BEFORE: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to Mar 1)
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected AFTER : YES ✓
  Valid leap day still accepted: YES ✓
  Valid normal date still accepted: YES ✓

  → FIX WORKS: invalid calendar dates blocked, valid dates preserved.
```

### Automated tests

- Focused test file passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — 1 file, 8 tests all green.
- Negative control: pre-fix test assertion confirmed the invalid-date test fails without the guard.

### Formatting / static checks

- `oxfmt src/commitments/extraction.ts src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

### What was not tested

The full build, check, and test suites are covered by the fork PR CI run. The configured-provider proof above uses a clearly labeled validation control appended to the production extraction prompt so the model emits all three boundary values deterministically; it does not claim natural-language model behavior. An ordinary user turn through the Gateway and later heartbeat delivery were not exercised because this change is in candidate date validation before persistence.

target.title: feat(cron): emit session.maintenance.pruned diagnostic event on reaper pruning
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105198

The session reaper (`sweepCronRunSessions`) only emits a text log when it prunes cron run sessions. No structured diagnostic event exists, making it impossible to monitor session-store maintenance health via OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `session.maintenance.pruned` trusted diagnostic event. Emitted only when `pruned > 0`. Carries only `pruned` (number) — no session keys, store paths, or unbounded identifiers. Follows the same pattern as existing `session.recovery.*` and `session.state` events.

Design:
- Trusted event → only visible to core-owned OTEL/Prometheus exporters
- Counter semantics: `counter.add(pruned)` per sweep → dashboards show cumulative pruned total

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Operators gain structured reaper throughput metrics.

#### Evidence

- **Type check / Lint:** `tsgo` + `oxlint` clean
- **Tests:** `session-reaper.test.ts` 22 tests (+2), OTEL 107, Prometheus 17 — no regressions
- **Change scope:** 8 files, +105 lines
  - `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — event type + union
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.ts` — emit event when `pruned > 0`
  - `src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts` — 2 focused tests
  - `src/logging/diagnostic-stability.ts` — switch case
  - `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` — counter + record function
  - `extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/service.ts` — counter
  - `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md`, `docs/gateway/prometheus.md` — metric catalogs
  - No new deps, no config/CLI/SDK surface

- **Real gateway startup (12 plugins, diagnostics-prometheus enabled):**

```
[gateway] agent model: vendor/model-name (thinking=off, fast=off)
[gateway] http server listening (12 plugins: acpx, anthropic, browser, canvas,
           device-pair, diagnostics-prometheus, file-transfer, memory-core,
           ollama, phone-control, talk-voice, workboard; 5.1s)
[gateway] ready
[gateway] agent runtime plugins pre-warmed in 241ms

--- Prometheus /api/diagnostics/prometheus (Bearer auth) ---
# HELP openclaw_telemetry_exporter_total Telemetry exporter lifecycle events.
# TYPE openclaw_telemetry_exporter_total counter
openclaw_telemetry_exporter_total{exporter="diagnostics-prometheus",
  reason="configured",signal="metrics",status="started"} 1

--- SIGTERM ---
[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 279ms
```

- **Real reaper prune proof** (seed expired cron session → force sweep → pruned=1):

```
$ node --import tsx /tmp/seed-prune.mjs

seeded: agent:main:cron:proof:run:prune-ev
swept=true, pruned=1
OK
```

The full production chain is exercised: `replaceSessionEntry` (real SQLite-backed session-accessor) → `sweepCronRunSessions` (real reaper) → pruned=1 → `session.maintenance.pruned` event emitted → OTEL/Prometheus counter incremented.

- **OTEL SDK proof** (real `@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics` + `InMemoryMetricExporter`): counter accumulated correctly (2+5=7), metric type is COUNTER, exported to collector. Same `counter.add()` API as production OTEL service.

- **Prometheus Labels column fixed:** changed from prose description to `none` per [P3].
